pillar: Demand Generation — beyond leads, measuring what matters
angle: Israeli founders are still reporting MQLs and funnel conversion like it's 2019, but the funnel they're tracking covers a shrinking minority of the actual buying journey. Ran's contrarian take: stop building better lead-scoring dashboards and start obsessing over whether AI chatbots recommend you at all — because by the time a 'lead' hits your CRM, the vendor shortlist was often already decided in a conversation you'll never see. This is a positioning problem wearing a demand-gen costume.

topic: The AI Budget Illusion: Why Spending More on AI Won't Fix a Broken Foundation
angle: CMOs are being praised for how much of their budget goes to AI, but that number is a vanity metric masking a foundation problem. Ran's contrarian take: AI spend without positioning clarity and clean data doesn't produce results, it produces confusion at scale and faster — and for Israeli B2B startups without a senior marketing leader, buying AI tools is often a subconscious substitute for doing the harder strategic work a CMO would force them to do.

topic: The Buying Committee Didn't Get More Complex — Your Positioning Did
angle: Every vendor report this month is screaming that B2B buying committees have exploded to 16 stakeholders, so the 'fix' being sold is more personalization tools, more content variants, more ABM tech. Ran's contrarian take: that's the wrong lesson. A 16-person buying committee is not a personalization problem, it's a positioning stress test — if your narrative isn't sharp enough for one stakeholder to repeat it accurately to fifteen others without you in the room, no amount of AI-generated content variants will save the deal. He'll use fractional-CMO scar tissue to show founders that the 'elevator retell' test matters more than the deck.
